name: OG.com ("OG") — Crypto.com's standalone prediction-market brand (launched Feb 3, 2026; operated via Crypto.com Derivatives North America (CDNA, the former Nadex) in the US and Foris Capital MU Limited, Mauritius FSC licence GB22200345, internationally)
positioning: Correction to the brief: OG.com is NOT a crypto casino today. It is Crypto.com's consumer prediction-markets platform on a premium two-letter domain, tagline "where it pays to be right," positioned as "the accessibility of a consumer app, engagement features of a social media network, and the rigor of an institutional-grade platform" (launch PR). It is sports-first — CEO Nick Lundgren: "Sports are the natural hub of prediction markets" — competing with Kalshi/Polymarket/Robinhood Predictions, differentiated by a parlay builder (unique among CFTC-regulated venues), planned margin trading, prop-market depth rivaling sportsbooks, and aggressive acquisition promos (up to $500 for first 1M users; "Trade $10, Get $10"; up-to-$100 milestone bonus). The honest read on "why it reads as a casino": its DNA is sportsbook, not slot-floor — parlays, player props, live in-play trading, payout-multiplier framing, and bonuses — and state regulators (Wisconsin suit 4/24/26 naming Crypto.com; Connecticut action) plus Better Markets explicitly characterize the category as unlicensed gambling. Sports contracts already pulled from NV/OH/MI/MD/MA/NJ/IL; platform unavailable in NY/AZ.
visualLanguage: Direct observation (desktop + mobile web, 2026-07-12): near-black #0D0D0D background, off-white #F7F9FA text, surfaces #16171C/#232328, brand orange #FF5300 (logo, active-tab underline, primary CTA "Sign up to trade", trade-slip multiplier, selected-chip outline), green reserved for stake-add chips (+$1/+$10/+$50), red for LIVE badges/error/losing lines, category/team accents (flags, MMA purple). Chart-forward: market pages open with a full-width multi-line probability chart with team-badge endpoints and big % pills. It reads "midnight trading terminal crossed with a sportsbook," not a neon casino: I observed NO jackpot/confetti/spin motifs, and notably no bonus banners on the logged-out web at all. The casino-adjacent signals that ARE present: pervasive LIVE red-dot badges with game clocks ("LIVE 2H • 50"), countdown urgency on upcoming events ("Begins in 2h 51m 56s"), constantly ticking percentages, a live win-amount ticker crawling over the price chart showing other users' results ("+$83.72 Harry Kane ⸱ Anytime Goal Scorer", "+$2.50 England", also losses like "-$12.75 Under 3.5"), and gambling-style payout framing in the ticket ("1.51x — $100 pays $151.51"). Cookie banner uses a dominant orange "Accept all" vs. lower-contrast reject — a dark-pattern emphasis.
typographyBrand: Logo is an all-caps, heavy, condensed "OG.COM" wordmark in #FF5300 (inline SVG). Computed styles: headings use "Funnel Display" at weight 600; body is "Funnel Sans" 16px (both modern geometric-humanist Google faces) — a contemporary, slightly sporty voice rather than a bank's. Numbers own the hierarchy: probability chips are the boldest, largest elements on every card; labels are secondary. Geometry is uniformly rounded-pill (search field, tabs, % chips, CTAs). Copy voice is terse imperative betting-speak: App Store subtitle "Find your edge. Trade it live."; PR tagline "where it pays to be right"; empty state "Pick an outcome from any market to get started." Percentages (not cents) are the default odds format, with a user-switchable odds-format control (gear icon) on the market page and trade slip.
navigationDiscovery: Top bar: logo | global "Search markets…" field | Trade Slip button (with count badge / alert state) | Log in | Sign up | hamburger. Below: a single horizontal category tab rail — Trending, Live, Sports, Crypto, Economics, Politics, Culture, Tech (routes to /companies), Climate — with orange active underline; on mobile it scrolls horizontally. Home = hero carousel of featured events ("1 of 4", live match with chart), then themed sections (e.g., "World Cup" with a "Bracket" tournament-visualization link), right rail with a promo slot ("Available throughout the U.S. Trade CFTC-regulated sports, culture, politics, and more"), a numbered TRENDING list (1–5, event + leading outcome + %), and a NEWS block. Market pages cross-sell via "Trending Markets" cards with countdowns and "See more events." Discovery model is category-first + trending-first + search; events advertise depth inline ("+906 more" markets on one match). No watchlist/portfolio visible logged out (assumed behind login).
marketCardAnatomy: Cards are event-level, not single-question. Home/mobile card contents (observed): category icon + label (trophy "WORLD CUP"), LIVE badge with red dot + game clock or start time ("Today, 3:00 am"), event title ("Norway vs England"), then outcome rows: flag/avatar, outcome name ("England to advance"), current score chip ("1"), and Yes/No probability chips in two labeled columns (75% / 26%) where each chip deep-links to a pre-filled buy/sell trade ("?contract=<id>:buy"). Footer link "+906 more" markets. Sub-market preview tiles inside cards on mobile ("Anytime Goal Scorer", "First Goalscorer" with player-shirt icons, "44+ players"). Market detail page: breadcrumb (SPORTS · WORLD CUP), live scoreboard header, share + odds-format buttons, multi-outcome probability chart with badge-labeled line endpoints (ENG 48% white / Tie 34% grey / NOR 19% red) with the win-ticker overlay, market-type filter (All / Game Lines / Players / Props), a line slider for Spread/Totals ("Current value: 1.5" with the full ladder 0.5–14.5 visible), Moneyline three-way, ~40 prop groups each with "Show more", a Timeline module (1 Event begins → 2 Event ends "Results are determined" → 3 Payment issued "Shortly after results are determined"), per-market "How It Works" resolution rules, and login-gated market chat. Notable honesty artifact: Yes+No chips sum to ~101% (both sides shown at ask), with no inline explanation of the spread.
tradeTicketClarity: Persistent right-rail "Trade Slip" on desktop; floating bottom dock on mobile ("Trade Slip · 1 can't combine") — selection state persists across pages (previously picked chip stays orange-outlined). Empty state coaches: "Your trade slip is empty. Pick an outcome from any market to get started." With one selection the header becomes an orange payout multiplier: "1.51x — $100 pays $151.51"; the leg shows outcome + side ("England to advance Yes"), live-updating price as % (66%→67% during observation), context lines (market type, event), and a remove icon. Stake entry = green quick-add chips (+$1/+$10/+$50) + $ input with unit dropdown; single CTA "Sign up to trade" (logged out). Parlay conflict handling is genuinely good: adding a live-market leg produced "Review your selections — 1 of 2 legs cannot be combined," the offending leg got a red-tinted card ("Below selection cannot be parlayed. Learn more"), and the CTA demoted to "Review your selections" instead of erroring at submit. Clarity gaps: no fee shown at this stage (fees are $0.02/contract to open, $0.02 to close early, waived at settlement — per OddsAssist teardown; not verifiable on-site logged out); the multiplier framing anchors on winnings rather than price/max-loss; % pricing hides the cents-based contract mechanics; the >100% Yes/No sum (spread) is never explained. An App Store review screams "40% FEES IS RIDICULOUS" — plausibly the flat $0.02 fee on cheap longshot contracts (e.g., 5¢), i.e., a regressive fee the ticket doesn't surface.
trustRiskSafety: Strongest point: resolution rules live ON the market page, per market type, in plain language with edge cases (own goals, abandoned matches: resume-within-48h or "settled as Event Cancelled", extra-time exclusions, player-participation rules), citing "Rule 14.67 Section (c) in the CDNA Rulebook" at nadex.com/rules plus the CFTC reg 40.2(a) filing PDF — best-in-class placement. The Timeline module sets payout expectations ("Payment issued shortly after results are determined"), though App Store reviews complain of ~1-week payout delays. Weaknesses: (1) Fees are nowhere in the logged-out UI or ticket. (2) Entity story is muddled — the page-bottom disclaimer says "Foris Capital MU Limited is authorised as an investment dealer and regulated by the Financial Services Commission Mauritius under Licence number GB22200345" while the same page's rules cite the CFTC-regulated CDNA rulebook; two regulatory identities on one page. (3) Responsible-use controls: none visible logged out — no deposit limits, self-exclusion, cool-off, or helpline anywhere I observed; ingame.com (as of 2026-04-15) reported none implemented, while FantasyLabs claims a "one-button lock" exists — unresolved conflict, but the absence of any logged-out RG signal while running bonuses + parlays + live props is exactly what regulators cite. (4) Bonus terms carry friction: "Trade $10, Get $10" requires a sub-80%-probability contract settled within 7 days of KYC; reviewers call the "$100 bonus" marketing deceptive. Withdrawals: ACH only ($1 min / $100k day / $500k month, no OG fees) vs. many instant deposit rails (card, Apple/Google Pay, Venmo) — asymmetry worth noting. 18+ age gate (App Store rating).
socialCommunity: Built-in and deliberate (PR: "trade, engage with others, and climb the leaderboard"). Observed: per-market chat on every event page, login-gated with the teaser "Log in or Sign up to start chatting"; a live ticker overlaying the price chart broadcasting other users' settled results with dollar amounts (wins AND losses: "+$68.00 England to advance", "-$12.75 Under 3.5") — social proof as ambient content; footer links to X, Discord, Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn. Reported but not directly observed: leaderboard for trader performance, tiered referral program (both sides earn: $100 volume → $10 each, up to $2,500 → $90 each within 30 days), and "OG Alpha," a conversational AI assistant (App Store description). Community is engagement-loop-oriented (chat + leaderboard + win feed) rather than knowledge-oriented (no visible forums, research notes, or resolution-dispute discussion).
mobileUsability: Genuinely well-executed. Mobile web (375px, observed): compact chrome — logo + single "Sign up / Log in" pill + hamburger; full-width search; horizontally scrollable category tabs; swipeable featured-event cards; Yes/No chips sized for thumbs in a two-column labeled grid; persistent bottom Trade Slip dock that carries live status text ("Trade Slip · 1 can't combine"); floating customer-support bubble; selection state synced from desktop session (orange outline persisted). Native app "OG.com: Predict Soccer & More" (developer OG Markets Limited): 4.4/5 from 970 ratings, Finance category, 18+, marketing "Simple. Fast. Powered by Regulated Markets"; reviews praise onboarding/bonuses, complain about fees, bonus fine print, and slow payouts. Caveat from direct observation: the always-live surfaces (streaming prices, tickers) made the renderer visibly busy — automated scrolls repeatedly timed out; plausible battery/perf cost on low-end phones (inference).
learnFrom: Resolution rules printed on the market page itself, per market type, in plain language with edge cases and a link to the exchange rulebook/regulatory filing — removes the 'where are the rules?' trust gap at exactly the moment of trade

Settlement Timeline module (Event begins → Event ends/Results determined → Payment issued) — three steps that set payout expectations inline; pair it with an honest SLA to avoid their 'week-long payout' complaints
Persistent cross-page trade slip with state (count badge, alert badge) and an instructive empty state — the slip is the app's spine on desktop rail and mobile bottom dock alike
Inline conflict handling in the ticket: incompatible parlay legs get a tinted card + one-line reason + 'Learn more', and the CTA demotes to 'Review your selections' instead of failing at submit
Line slider for spread/total families ('Current value: 1.5' across a 0.5–14.5 ladder) — one control to browse many strike contracts without card sprawl
Every probability chip is a deep link that pre-fills the ticket (?contract=<id>:buy) — one-tap from browse to ticket, shareable/campaign-able URLs
Odds-format toggle (percent / other formats via gear icon) serving both bettor and trader mental models
Chart-first market pages: multi-outcome probability history with badge-labeled line endpoints doubles as narrative ('what happened in this match') — far more informative than a static % chip
Numbered Trending list + search-first header to concentrate liquidity on a few hot markets
Mobile chrome discipline: one auth pill, scrollable tab rail, thumb-scale Yes/No grid, bottom-docked ticket — no bottom-nav clutter
avoid: Payout-multiplier as the ticket's headline ('1.51x — $100 pays $151.51' in brand orange) — pure betting-slip framing that anchors on winnings, hides price/max-loss, and is the single biggest 'this is gambling' signal in the UI
Live win-ticker of other users' dollar results crawling over the price chart — celebration/social-proof pattern that manufactures FOMO; including losses doesn't neutralize it
Countdown-timer urgency on market cards ('Begins in 2h 51m 56s') — trading deadlines can be shown as timestamps without a ticking clock

Volume-milestone bonus ladders ('Trade $10 Get $10' with sub-80%-probability and 7-day settlement conditions; 'up to $100'; 'first 1M users up to $500') — churn-inducing wagering-requirement mechanics that earned 'deceptive' App Store reviews

Hiding fees from the trade ticket: flat $0.02/contract is regressive on longshots (2¢ on a 5¢ contract = 40% of stake — the exact '40% FEES IS RIDICULOUS' review); show effective fee % in-ticket before confirm
Yes/No prices that sum to ~101% with no inline spread explanation — sophisticated users notice, everyone else is silently overcharged
Split regulatory identity on one page (Mauritius FSC disclaimer at the bottom, CFTC/CDNA rulebook in the rules) — pick one clear licensing story per geography and state it in the footer

Zero visible responsible-use surface while running parlays + live props + bonuses: no deposit limits, self-exclusion, cool-off, or helpline logged out — this is the gap state AGs are suing over; ship limits and cool-off at launch and put the link in the footer
Prop sprawl: ~40 prop groups per match including junk markets quoted at 99% ('To Score 5+ Goals') — thin liquidity, fee/spread harvesting, and cognitive noise
Cookie-consent dark pattern (dominant orange 'Accept all', muted reject)
Login-gated teasers on every social surface ('Log in or Sign up to start chatting') — conversion nagging that cheapens community
Always-streaming everything (prices, tickers, charts) without perf budget — our session saw renderer contention; costs low-end mobile users

INFERENCE: 'reads sportsbook-dark, not casino-bright' (from absence of bonus banners/confetti in logged-out web — the logged-in experience may differ); the '40% fees' review being the flat $0.02 fee on cheap contracts; geo-split entity presentation (browser session showed Mauritius disclaimer alongside CDNA rules — possibly a global page mixing both regimes); perf cost of streaming UI. SECONDARY (not verified on-site): fee schedule ($0.02/contract), deposit/withdrawal rails and limits, referral tiers, bonus fine print, state availability list, leaderboard and OG Alpha features (press release/App Store only — not seen in UI), payout-delay complaints. UNRESOLVED CONFLICT: responsible-trading tools — FantasyLabs claims a one-button lock exists; ingame.com (2026-04-15) says none implemented; I observed zero RG surface logged out; treat as 'minimal at best'. ASSUMPTION: logged-in surfaces (portfolio, bonus UI, leaderboard, chat) unobserved — no account was created per policy. CORRECTION TO BRIEF: the premise 'OG.com is a crypto casino/gaming brand' is wrong as of 2026-07-12 — it is Crypto.com's regulated prediction-market brand (CDNA/CFTC in US; Foris Capital MU/Mauritius FSC internationally); the casino-pattern audit still applies because the product deliberately imports sportsbook mechanics (parlays, props, multiplier payouts, bonuses, live urgency) and multiple state regulators are litigating it as gambling.
